scope: Explicit footprint-purpose/geometry assessments for the generated WirePad exports. Unlisted components default to not reviewed. Generated 3D accuracy is independently approximate under the current box-based WRL exporter; external CAD links are not imported.

assessments.evidence: Dedicated package drawings and example land patterns were source checked in the November 8 radio expansion. The QFN footprints retain the documented pad geometry but omit thermal vias and paste segmentation.

Dedicated Ai-Thinker specifications and manufacturer PADS libraries were reviewed for these exact module variants. Ra-05 pad 10 follows the dimensioned pitch rather than the inconsistent ASC coordinate. Base SC/SCH patterns exclude extra -P contacts.

Dedicated EBYTE manuals/mechanical drawings verify electrical contact positions and numbered native lands. DIP entries cover seven electrical contacts only and omit three mechanical fixing holes; this is not a complete assembly footprint.
Raytac manufacturer libraries and layout drawings supply the module land dimensions and coordinates. Antenna, top-layer and RF keepouts remain an assembly/layout responsibility.
Seeed XIAO KiCad footprints supply the native SMD contact coordinates and dimensions. This mark covers the stated source geometry, not antenna clearance or fabrication approval.

Published Adafruit/SparkFun EAGLE files were reviewed for native header, terminal and connector solder-tail centers, sizes and numbering. These references omit mounting holes and include onboard connector tails; they are not complete mating patterns.

Manufacturer board CAD supplies the exposed contact coordinates and terminal numbering. The export is a source-board contact carrier, including service pads, not a full PCB or mating connector reproduction; reverse-side SMD contacts are exported on F.Cu.
The manufacturer DXF supplies native P1/P2/P3/P4 electrical hole centers and drill sizes. Board mounting holes are not exported and small-part/3D details remain approximate.

Existing family source notes and physical-contact audit records identify manufacturer EAGLE contact-coordinate references. This documentation review did not repeat the CAD audit and does not claim a complete mating/production footprint.

AMASS PCB drawings verify the 7.20 mm terminal pitch and 4.60 mm finished-hole geometry. WirePad chooses the copper diameter, so the mark is scoped to a contact/hole reference rather than a fully manufacturer-derived land pattern.

The listed entries explicitly limit their own footprint exports to reference carriers, approximate geometry, photo-derived placement or off-board/cable terminations. This records the existing limitation; source-checked pin maps do not make those footprints mating patterns. IDs are listed explicitly so new entries do not inherit this assessment.
Generic discrete parts and connector examples use selected nominal package sizes/pitches. The family does not bind every generic identity to an exact manufacturer orderable part or revision.

The original radio family uses shared package/reference host-land definitions and chosen extensions. This documentation review does not establish full manufacturer land-pattern accuracy for these legacy entries.

Generated WRL bodies are independently approximate.

Arduino V0.3 schematics, Gerbers and drill files establish source coordinates for headers, Qwiic socket tails/retainers and fifteen rear fixture pads on each Modulino. Separate mirrored rear views retain eight NC and seven wired service contacts. The exported carrier includes source contact geometry and repeated grounded retainer pads, not a complete production or mating PCB; generated 3D remains approximate.

PJRC manufacturer cards, mechanical drawings and numbered test-point references establish these exact Teensy contact functions. Rear-view transformation and physical pad order are explicit. Exported footprints are selected reference wire/contact carriers rather than audited complete manufacturer production or mating land patterns; generated WRL models are approximate.

Dedicated Pico 2/Pico 2 W manufacturer datasheets verify the source header, SWD, test-point and USB-shell ground centers, with mirrored rear views retaining each TP number. Selected host lands do not reproduce the asymmetric manufacturer SMT paste stencil or complete production land pattern. Four USB-shell grounds repeat the matching ground electrical terminal. Generated WRL remains approximate.

Debug Probe Rev2 source schematic and numbered rear photograph verify 26 actual test points (TP4 absent), own SWD header and target-facing socket contacts. Artwork is photo-scaled and the native cable/contact carrier is representative rather than a manufacturer mating land pattern. Internal probe MCU signals remain distinct from target outputs and LED rails. Generated WRL remains approximate.
